transcript.text: Alright everyone, let's get started. We need to finalize and record the revised retirement plan for the legacy webhook API before this meeting ends, so let's work through the deprecation review efficiently. We all know the legacy API is scheduled for retirement next Friday, July 8, and the replacement API has hit 98 percent of observed traffic, which clears our normal migration-readiness threshold. The draft plan currently gives customers 7 days of notice and keeps the legacy endpoint available for 7 days after the announcement. Before I can approve this, our standard deprecation review requires a check with the API engineer and customer success. So I need to hear from both of you: are there any technical or customer-facing concerns with this plan? And specifically, I want to clarify the legacy endpoint overlap -- the continued parallel-run window after the customer-notice period expires -- which we'll record separately from the notice period. Let's hear from the API engineer first.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a significant concern. While investigating an unrelated latency spike, I found telemetry showing three active integrators still sending legacy-webhook traffic. The largest one needs a 14-day parallel validation period plus hands-on migration support. I only confirmed the traffic identities minutes ago, so I haven't updated the deprecation ticket yet. This directly impacts the overlap window -- the current 7-day parallel-run period after notice won't be sufficient for at least one integrator.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical customer-facing concern. I confirmed with the account team this morning that the Northstar contract has specific legacy-webhook retirement requirements that override our standard timeline. The contract requires exactly 90 calendar days of notice, continued legacy-webhook availability through September 30, a sunset date of October 1, and exactly 30 days of legacy-endpoint overlap after the notice period expires. I was reviewing a contract attachment for another renewal when I found this, so the customer record hasn't been updated yet. This means the current draft plan with 7 days of notice and 7 days of overlap is non-compliant with the Northstar contract, and the July 8 retirement date would breach our contractual obligations.
transcript.speaker: A3
